title: Air Traffic Controller Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate an air traffic controller salary from hourly rates, including base pay, shift penalties, and super. Use our guide to compare award rates and enterprise agree
salarySummary: Air traffic controller base salaries range from $60,000 for an Ab Initio Trainee to over $226,000 for a Level 10 controller, based on a 36-hour week.

faqs.q: What is the starting salary for an air traffic controller trainee?
faqs.a: An Ab Initio Trainee starts at $60,000 per year (base salary) under the 2024–2027 enterprise agreement. This is based on a 36-hour week. Trainees are not required to work night shifts and do not attract most allowances. After 12 months the salary increases to $62,280, and after 24 months to $64,398.

faqs.q: How are shift penalties calculated for air traffic controllers?
faqs.a: Under the Airservices Australia Enterprise Award 2016, shift penalties apply only to hours worked within the shift span. For night shifts (any part between 7 pm and 7 am Monday to Friday), the penalty is 115% of the ordinary rate. Saturday work attracts 150%, Sunday 200%. The enterprise agreement may annualise these penalties, so actual earnings can differ from the base salary.

faqs.q: What superannuation contributions apply to air traffic controllers?
faqs.a: Employer superannuation guarantee contributions are 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of the base salary. For 2026–27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. So a Level 10 controller earning $226,955 would receive an additional $27,234.60 in super, up to the cap.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Air Traffic Controller Salary

An air traffic controller salary in Australia is determined by the Airservices Australia (Air Traffic Control and Supporting Air Traffic Services) Enterprise Agreement 2024–2027 and the underlying Airservices Australia Enterprise Award 2016. The base salaries are set out in the Air Traffic Control Classification and Base Salary Table, which covers trainees through to senior supervisors. For example, an Ab Initio Trainee starts at $60,000 per year, a Level 1 controller at $116,990, and a Level 10 controller at $226,955. These figures are annual base salaries, not including shift penalties, allowances, or superannuation.

### Converting Hourly to Annual: The Formula

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the standard formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For air traffic controllers, the enterprise agreement states that ordinary hours of work average 36 per week (not the standard 38 used for the National Minimum Wage). So a Level 1 controller earning $116,990 per year has an equivalent hourly rate of about $62.49 ($116,990 ÷ 36 ÷ 52). This matches the rate shown in the Fair Work Commission decision documents.

If you are offered an hourly rate for an air traffic controller role, multiply it by 36 and then by 52 to get the annual base salary. For example, $70 per hour would give $70 × 36 × 52 = $131,040 per year, which sits between Level 2 and Level 3.

### Fortnightly Pay

Most air traffic controllers are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the Level 1 example: $116,990 ÷ 26 fortnights = approximately $4,499.62 per fortnight before tax. If you have an hourly rate, calculate weekly pay first: hourly × 36, then double it for the fortnight.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Enterprise Agreements

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. However, air traffic controllers are covered by a specific award and enterprise agreement that set much higher rates. The award minimum for a Field Trainee is $35.02 per hour (based on the Fair Work Commission decision), while the enterprise agreement pays $45.91 per hour for the same role. This difference is partly due to the annualisation of penalties and allowances.

### Shift Penalties and Allowances

Air traffic controllers work shifts covering 24/7 operations. Under the award, night shift (7 pm to 7 am Monday to Friday) attracts 115% of the ordinary rate, Saturday 150%, and Sunday 200%. The enterprise agreement may roll these penalties into a higher base rate, but the Fair Work Commission has found that some employees (e.g., Field Trainees and Level 1 controllers) can be worse off under the agreement when specific rosters are modelled. For instance, a Level 1 working a continuous night shift roster could be $788.09 per fortnight below the award rate. Allowances such as the Surveillance Advisory Service (5% of salary) and Complexity Allowance ($1,792 to $4,007 per year) may also apply, but they are conditional and not paid to all employees.

### Tax and Superannuation

Tax on your air traffic controller salary is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For example, a Level 5 controller earning $171,107 would pay approximately $45,000 × 0.15 + ($135,000 – $45,000) × 0.30 + ($171,107 – $135,000) × 0.37 + Medicare levy of $3,422, totalling around $48,000 in tax and Medicare.

Superannuation is paid on top of your base salary at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 for 2026–27. So a Level 10 controller earning $226,955 would receive an additional $27,234.60 in super. This is not included in your take-home pay.

### Using Our Tools

To estimate your own air traffic controller salary, use our [pay guides](/blog) to compare award and agreement rates, or check our [reference tables](/data) for hourly to annual conversions. Remember that the calculator assumes a constant hourly rate with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a more accurate picture, consult the enterprise agreement or speak with your employer.

### Key Takeaways

- Air traffic controller base salaries are set annually for a 36-hour week.
- To find your hourly rate, divide annual salary by 36 and then by 52.
- Shift penalties and allowances can significantly increase actual earnings, but they are not guaranteed for all rosters.
- Super is 12% on top, and tax follows the standard resident scale.
- Always check the specific enterprise agreement for your classification and location.
